The editor runs in a browser and as a desktop application. This page lists what is built and tested, not every environment the code might happen to work in.

## Browsers

“Tested automatically” means the browser suite runs against this engine on every pull request. An engine that is not listed is not tested and is not claimed to work.

| Browser engine | Tested automatically |
| --- | --- |
| Chromium (Chrome, Edge) | Yes |
| Firefox | Yes |
| WebKit (Safari) | Yes |

## Desktop packages

| Operating system | Architecture | Packages | Packaging check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | arm64 | AppImage; Debian package | Packaged and started in an automated smoke test |
| Linux | x64 | AppImage; Debian package | Packaged and started in an automated smoke test |
| Windows | arm64 | Installer; Zip archive | Packaged and started in an automated smoke test |
| Windows | x64 | Installer; Zip archive | Packaged and started in an automated smoke test |
| macOS | arm64 | Disk image | Packaged and started in an automated smoke test |

## Motionscaper development qualification

Focused Chromium workflows cover editing, history, portable save/reopen, offline assets, preview and delivery. A bounded Chromium, Firefox and Linux WebKit fixture additionally verifies retained fonts, authored keys, same-engine PNG pixels and offline reopen after origin shutdown; Chromium and Firefox produce actual VP9 WebM, while Linux WebKit refuses its independently reproduced native encoder crash. Whole-frame hashes are not claimed identical between engines. Packaged Linux x64 checks cover the own-origin shell, bounded native project files, saved-file composition updates and ProRes 4444 with PCM24 audio. Actual software-rendered 2.5D and offline linked-composition scenes agree with decoded native output within declared color/alpha bounds and retain exact timing. Focused Chromium linked-scene checks verify complete CPU finishing preview when WebGL is unavailable or loses its context, restoration and offline reopen; animated timeline-image layers mixed with retained scenes also pass WebGL2-disabled playback, NTSC seek/export comparison in both painter orders and project replacement. GPU-only inherited Frame adjustment effects explicitly refuse when WebGL2 is unavailable. A complete local Linux x64 aggregate passes all three source-bound packaged workflows; candidate/nightly Linux jobs now enforce them with a separate verified test-only reference artifact. Other target execution remains unqualified. Native cold/warm file opening, reviewed archive collisions, exact opaque custody and renderer-reload reissue also have actual packaged Linux x64 evidence. Complete Motion-to-AE rendered transfer passes full-quality frame/digest checks and retains the original project and all source media; installed AE import remains unqualified. Manual update-check tests verify bounded own-tag selection and explicit release links. These bounded fixtures do not establish behavior at maximum workload limits. Full regression, hardware GPU, macOS Safari, the remaining native targets, signing/release-update qualification and installed After Effects interchange remain unqualified for the first Motionscaper release.

## Where a capability can run

Capabilities are grouped by what they need from the platform. See [Product capabilities](/reference/generated/product-capabilities/) for which capabilities each product enables.

| Tier | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| `web-core` | Works in every supported browser, with no optional platform feature required. |
| `web-enhanced` | Works in a browser that provides the newer storage and media features the capability needs. |
| `electron-enhanced` | Works in the browser, and the desktop application does more with it. |
| `electron-only` | Needs the desktop application, because a browser cannot reach what the capability uses. |
